Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
240 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Cold temperatures and areas of freezing fog expected this morning, 
  followed by mostly dry weather today.

* A weak storm will bring periods of light valley rain and snow 
  tonight through Sunday, with minor travel impacts in the Sierra.

* Holiday travel will be most ideal Monday into Tuesday, disrupted
  by another storm Tuesday night or Wednesday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A bitterly cold morning is in store in the wake of our latest 
winter storm, with overnight temperatures falling into the single 
digits to teens. Cold-prone locales (e.g., Truckee, Bodie, 
Bridgeport, Mammoth Lakes) will flirt with or perhaps drop below 
zero through early morning. Clearing skies and fresh snow on the 
ground will support areas of freezing fog across NE California and
E Sierra valleys tonight into early Saturday morning. Elsewhere, 
patchy freezing fog will be possible in the Mono Basin, Carson 
Valley, and the Carson sink. Drive slow and leave extra space 
between cars if encountering any freezing fog banks this morning.

A pair of upper trough passages will comprise this weekend's storm, 
with rain and snow accompanying each passage. The first shortwave 
pivots through the Pacific Northwest tonight, dragging a band of 
light showers into NE California and far NW Nevada. The second 
trough will be the wetter of the two (albeit still weak), increasing 
shower coverage across the Sierra and W Nevada late Sunday morning 
and afternoon. Ridge winds will also become elevated tonight into 
early Sunday with gusts of 50-70 mph posing aviation and backcountry 
recreation impacts.  

The storm quickly departs to the east Monday morning, leaving 2-5" 
of snow along the Sierra crest/at pass level with up to 3" at 
Truckee/lake level and lower Mono communities W of US-395. Certainly 
not a major winter storm by any means, but even light snow can cause 
travel disruptions so be prepared if heading to the mountains this 
weekend. Spillover into W Nevada is more uncertain with guidance 
favoring areas north of Reno/I-80 on Sunday. However, some scenarios 
feature the best spillover farther south, which would bring showers 
into Reno and the I-80 corridor. Should this happen, snow levels 
below 5500 ft would allow a dusting to 1" of snow for foothill 
communities such as Virginia City and Galena (40-60% chance). 
Daytime heating -- perhaps coupled with warming from an advertised
shadowing effect -- will likely lift snow levels to 4500-5000 ft 
at the onset of shower activity, falling below valley floors in 
the evening. Thus, expect a rain or rain-snow mix to transition to
light snow Sunday evening, with a trace of snow possible on 
elevated and grassy surfaces. 

Monday into Tuesday morning will offer the best opportunity to 
travel across the Sierra for Thanksgiving before another storm 
deteriorates Sierra road conditions late Tuesday and Wednesday. 
Increasing winds will also present aviation impacts leading up to 
the holiday. However, keep in mind that fresh snow and continued 
chilly nights will renew AM freezing fog and icy road potential 
during this timeframe. The midweek storm will be a warmer one with 
higher snow levels, keeping the snow in the mountains and returning 
rain to valley and foothill areas. The forecast for Thanksgiving 
onward is a bit more uncertain, but ensembles suggest that 
Thanksgiving Day and the Friday after will be dry and mild with 
storms returning later in the holiday weekend (Nov 28-29). 

-Salas

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions prevail today, with increasing mid to 
upper clouds this afternoon and evening. SW FL100 winds increase to 
30 kts after 00z this afternoon, introducing LLWS and mountain wave 
turbulence concerns that last through Sunday morning.

Regional Outlook: FZFG and LIFR conditions prevail at KTRK through 
16-17Z this morning before dissipating. Elsewhere, there is a low 
chance of FZFG at/near KCXP-KMEV. Increasing SW FL100 winds will 
introduce LLWS and mountain wave turbulence issues after 21z this
afternoon. Low chances (10-30%) of -SHSN return to KTRK-KTVL 
after 06Z. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: Increasing chances for light snow across E 
Sierra terminals between 18Z Sunday and 03Z Monday, occasionally 
reducing CIGS/VIS to MVFR or briefly IFR conditions. Chances of rain 
or a rain-snow mix increase to 20-40% late Sunday morning for KRNO-
KCXP-KMEV, becoming -SN Sunday night. A period of dry weather Monday 
into Tuesday will allow better flight conditions, before the next
storm arrives Tuesday night.

-Salas
